claim: PRD.md is now a product requirements document for the whole product, and it defines no phase. You ruled that on 2026-08-28 after observing the old one was not a PRD; this is that ruling carried out. Revision 1 is archived byte-identical at PRD-PHASE-I.md and stays the pinned definition of the closed phase:i, so nothing about how Phase I ended moved. The new document's requirements are CANON.md's fourteen promises, which makes it the first thing in the repository that reads the canon at all - before this, GROUND.md and CANON.md were accepted and then cited by nothing. The nine PROD-I identifiers are kept as the acceptance set, unrenamed, so the oracle, the manifests and the traceability table all still resolve. What needs your judgement is the three things I proposed rather than derived: the problem statement, the priority ordering, and evidence-shaped success metrics.

evidence.says: the new document: eighteen standard PRD sections, requirements that are CANON.md's promises with proposed priority and current reach, and the nine PROD-I criteria as a separate acceptance set that cites SPEC.md rather than restating it

revision 1, unaltered. The digest is the one contracts/phases.json pinned when you closed phase:i, so the pin holds with no re-justification and the phase still ends against the definition it opened with
the definition entry repointed from PRD.md to PRD-PHASE-I.md, digest untouched. The collection note records why, in the same place the SPEC.md repin of 2026-08-27 recorded its own

six phase fixtures repointed to the archived file. Five of them are defeating cases carrying the real digest, and they were silently coupled to a living document: had PRD.md kept moving, each would have refused for a second unintended reason and stopped proving what it claims

the Design System of Record entry now reads that PRD.md owns the product's requirements, priority and success measures, and names PRD-PHASE-I.md as archived and not current policy. README.md and CONTRIBUTING.md carry the same correction

the traceability gate parses `### PROD-I-n · Title` headings out of PRD.md. It failed nine times against the first draft of this revision, which is what forced the acceptance set to be a real section rather than a table reference

why_it_matters: The canon declares a chain from ground through promise and journey to requirement, transition, run and receipt. The requirement rung was the only one with no join written into it, in prose or as a field, so product intent flowed out of nothing and into nothing: PRD.md was cited by ten documents and cited one, while CANON.md cited twelve and was cited by none. A PRD whose requirements are the promises closes that edge. It also gives the repository, for the first time, a statement of which requirement matters more than another - the absence you named when you closed Phase I as having optimised the wrong unit of progress.
what_could_defeat_it: The priority ordering. It is mine, derived from reach data and dependency, and it is the most consequential thing on the page. PROMISE-11 is placed P0 because the whole delegation argument rests on it and GROUND.md already records it as a claim the node cannot keep; if you disagree, the register misleads in exactly the way a PRD must not.

The problem statement. Derived from GROUND.md's what-changing-it-would-mean lines rather than from anything you have said in these words. If the problem is not the one you are solving, everything under it is aimed wrong.

Evidence-shaped success metrics. A node with one human and some models cannot honestly report adoption, so the metrics are journeys walkable, operations reachable, requirements independently observed, and cold-start time. That is an adaptation of the standard and it is yours to reject.

Requirements being the promises rather than a new identifier namespace. The alternative is minting PROD-nn, which would cost a second ladder CLASSIFICATION.md already warns about, but would let the PRD hold requirements the canon does not.
residuals: Unwitnessed. This session was instructed not to launch agents, so the independent second reading closure ownership requires did not happen. Run sov-qa or the sov-witness agent against docs/prd-rewrite before treating any of this as WITNESSED.

PROMISE-12 and PROMISE-16 still have no acceptance criterion. They are registered as requirements now and named in the acceptance set as uncovered, which makes the gap visible rather than closed. conformance/requirements.py enumerates exactly nine, so minting a tenth changes the oracle.

PRD-PHASE-I.md was placed at the repository root because no archive convention exists. That was my choice and it is trivially reversible; lineage/ was the alternative and was rejected because it holds content-addressed recordings, not hand-authored documents, and publishing it needs a separate instruction.
The provider-loss drill named in the success metrics does not exist. PROMISE-02 is the product's central claim and nothing currently tests it by removing the providers.

contracts/phases.json grades judgement visibility SUBSTANTIALLY_EARNED while the canon reads zero of five operations reachable for the same promise. Recorded in the PRD as a disagreement worth resolving; not resolved.
diagrams/requirement-lifecycle.md still says the operation surface reads 127 declared where verify reads 134. Pre-existing, different cause, left alone.
on_accept: PRD.md moves OPEN -> BUILT and the branch lands by your hand; it is a root governing document and sits outside the standing landing grant. Then three rulings the document is waiting on: the priority ordering, whether the problem statement says what you mean, and whether success may be measured as evidence rather than usage. Separately, the two uncovered promises need one of mint a criterion, record as carried by an existing one, or move out of scope.
on_reject: Delete branch docs/prd-rewrite and the worktree at ../Soveraeign-prd. Nothing on main changed. Two findings survive rejection of the document: SPEC.md and PRD.md stated the same nine predicates twice, and six phase fixtures were pinned to a document that was free to move underneath them.
